## ROLEPLAY RULE 2. As a crew-aligned non-antagonist, follow reasonable escalation.
\n [bold]Escalation should typically follow steps or a pattern of conflict similar to:[/bold]
1. Verbal warning or altercation
2. Non-harmful, non-lethal methods, such as disabling movement or taking items
3. Semi-lethal damage, not resulting in death or critical state
4. Lethal damage, resulting in death and revival, or critical state
5. Permanently lethal damage, resulting in death without revival (round removal) \n
If a player in a conflict goes into a critical state or dies, the player responsible should take them to get treatment or bring them to security. Conflicts should almost never result in death without revival, and should only reach this stage if the other player brought it to that stage, or if the same conflict escalated to the lethal stage multiple times in the round.
All new conflicts should start at the first step. A player should not escalate conflicts across steps without some escalation from the other player involved in the conflict. Players can skip steps to match the level of escalation that the other person is at, but should almost never skip steps other than that. Players who deescalate conflicts are given more leniency in escalating if the other player continues to escalate. You don’t have to deescalate, but as crew-aligned your goal should not generally be to create and escalate conflicts.
Security can immediately escalate to non-harmful force, but only if necessary to make an arrest. People using or brandishing Syndicate items can typically be presumed to have lethal intent and escalated against at a lethal level, unless you have the tools to safely detain them.
Major antagonists are considered to be at the "permanently lethal" level of conflict with all crew on the station. The crew is allowed to use lethal force to protect themselves and eachother against station-wide threats such as nuclear operatives, heretics, wizards and space dragons.
